paragraphs: Rabbi Levi, son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani.

Yuchasin and Seder HaDorot cite this from Berakhot 28b. Hyman says that the old printings indeed read this way, but it is a printing error. The reading should follow the correction in the Vilna printing: Rabbi Levi says that the blessing concerning the Sadducees was instituted at Yavneh. Asked what it corresponds to, Rabbi Levi answers: [according to] Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, it corresponds to “The God of glory thunders,” since Rabbi Hillel derives the eighteen blessings from the psalm “Ascribe to the Lord,” etc.; [according to] Rav Yosef, it corresponds to “One” in the Shema; [according to] Rabbi Tanchum reporting Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, it corresponds to the small vertebra in the spine. Hyman regards this as clear.
Hyman says that the author of Otzar Yisrael likewise erred in this.

notes.text: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani is explicitly named in the checked passage. Hyman inserts “according to” to explain the blessing’s correspondence; this is his reconstruction of the printed attribution, not an adopted father–son identity.

The consulted Berakhot 28b separately names Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, Rav Yosef and Rabbi Tanchum reporting Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. In the extra-blessing passage Levi addresses Hillel’s position; this is not proof that Levi is Shmuel’s son. Hyman’s confident old-print/Vilna correction and Otzar Yisrael criticism remain attributed, since the exact old printings were not inspected.
